Given that $f(x)=(x-2)^{2},$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (2,\infty )$

II. $x\in (-1,5)$

III. $x\in (-\infty ,2]$

The graph of the function $f(x)=(x-2)^{2},$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

2\. Translate it by $2$ units  to  the right  $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/1e3ac550e35a3dc93b3e26e5834f763847b04f5133de02e368124f54dd2b9dd6.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-1,5).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/3ebb316ca122b6786b8ef501fc7c56f8e0e68c8cfc32e5801c493d38382fc26c.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the intervals $x\in (2,\infty )$  and $x\in (-\infty ,2].$  On these intervals, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/86c7c9cacc7a3868565f33130563ffed0ca423aa087e76cc08d103ea171822ed.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
